description: Romano-British settlement which appears to be occupied from the 1st CE until the end of the 4th CE, though there is some evidence of earlier Iron Age occupation. Finds including an altar have been used to suggest that a shrine was present on the site, but which structure it was, if it was a structure at all is uncertain.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Haymes, Cleeve Hill (Gloucestershire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
Rawes. “The Romano-British Settlement at Haymes, Cleeve Hill, near Cheltenham.” Trans Bristol and Gloucestershire Archaeological Society 104 (1986).
